title: Module pullback and pushforward adjunction on arbitrary ringed topoi
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites, with sheaves of commutative rings $R,S$, and let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a morphism of topoi, an adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ with $u^{-1}$ preserving finite limits, equipped with a ring map $c:u^{-1}R\to S$. On module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] put $u^*M=S\otimes_{u^{-1}R}u^{-1}M$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For an $S$-module sheaf $H$, give $u_*H$ its $R$-module structure via the adjunct $R\to u_*S$ of $c$. There are canonical bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_S(u^*M,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,u_*H)$, natural in $M,H$. Thus the displayed tensor-formula pullback is left adjoint to this module pushforward.

proof.text: Write $L=u^{-1}$, $V=u_*$, with unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$, and $A=LR$. Besides the assumed finite-product preservation of $L$, $V$ preserves finite products: for every sheaf $T$, the given adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(T,V(H_1\times H_2))$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(LT,H_1)\times\operatorname{Hom}(LT,H_2)$ and hence with $\operatorname{Hom}(T,VH_1)\times\operatorname{Hom}(T,VH_2)$; the terminal-object case is the same with a singleton. Apply these canonical product identifications to the ring operations of $R$ and to the additive and scalar operations of $M$ and $H$. Functoriality carries each defining equation (associativity, distributivity, zero and unit) to the same equation after applying $L$ or $V$. This constructs the $A$-module $LM$ and the $VS$-module $VH$, and sends linear maps to linear maps, as required by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

Let $F$ be any $A$-module sheaf and endow $VF$ with its $R$-action via $\eta_R:R\to VA$. The set-sheaf adjunction sends $\alpha:LM\to F$ to $\beta=V\alpha\circ\eta_M$. For scalar multiplication write $\mu_M:R\times M\to M$ and $\mu_F:LR\times F\to F$. Naturality gives the explicit mates $\operatorname{adj}(\alpha\circ L\mu_M)=\beta\circ\mu_M$ and $\operatorname{adj}(\mu_F\circ(\mathrm{id}_{LR}\times\alpha))=V\mu_F\circ(\eta_R\times\beta)$ for scalar multiplication. For addition replace the last expression by $V\mu_F\circ(\beta\times\beta)$; for zero use the terminal object. These formulas follow by inserting $V\alpha\eta_M$ and using that the component of $\eta$ on a product has components $\eta$ on its factors. Thus, by injectivity of the given hom-set bijection, $\alpha$ preserves addition, zero and scalar multiplication if and only if $\beta$ does. This proves, in both directions, a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_A(LM,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,VF)$ from the module morphism definition [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

proof.text: Restrict the $S$-action on $H$ along $c:A\to S$ and call the resulting $A$-module $H_c$. The $R$-action on $VH_c$ in the preceding step is $V\mu_H\circ(Vc\times\mathrm{id})\circ(\eta_R\times\mathrm{id})$. Since the adjunct of $c$ is exactly $c^\sharp=Vc\circ\eta_R$, this is the action of $R$ on the module pushforward specified in the statement. Its underlying sheaf is $VH$; no replacement of the given geometric morphism or coefficient rings is involved.

For an $A$-module sheaf $G$ on $\mathcal D$, let $P(W)=S(W)\otimes_{A(W)}G(W)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scalar-extension-hom], a sectionwise $A(W)$-linear map $\lambda_W:G(W)\to H(W)$ uniquely extends to the $S(W)$-linear map $s\otimes g\mapsto s\lambda_W(g)$ on $P(W)$. These maps commute with restriction along $W\to W_0$: both ways on a pure tensor give $s|_W\lambda_W(g|_W)$, by the semilinear restrictions of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Conversely a presheaf map gives $\lambda_W(g)=\psi_W(1\otimes g)$, which commutes with restrictions because $1$ restricts to $1$. The inverse identities hold sectionwise by the cited bijection. This gives a bijection from $S$-linear presheaf maps $P\to H$ to $A$-linear sheaf maps $G\to H_c$.

By [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $S\otimes_A G$ is precisely the module sheafification $P^\#$. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], every $S$-linear map $P\to H$ factors uniquely through $P^\#$ because $H$ is a sheaf of $S$-modules. Therefore the preceding bijection is $\operatorname{Hom}_S(S\otimes_A G,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(G,H_c)$. Its forward map is restriction to $1\otimes g$, and its inverse is the unique sheaf extension of $s\otimes g\mapsto s\lambda(g)$.

Take $G=LM$ in step 5 and then compose with step 2 for $F=H_c$, using the action identification of step 3. This gives exactly $\operatorname{Hom}_S(S\otimes_{LR}LM,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,u_*H)$. For an $R$-linear $a:M_0\to M$, precomposition on the tensor side by $\mathrm{id}_S\otimes La$ becomes precomposition by $La$ after restriction to $1\otimes g$, then precomposition by $a$ after applying the naturality of the given set adjunction. For an $S$-linear $b:H\to H_0$, postcomposition becomes postcomposition by $b$ after that restriction (since $b(sx)=sb(x)$), then by $Vb$ under the given adjunction. The uniqueness of the sheaf extension proves the same identities for the inverse maps. Thus the bijection is natural in both variables and defines the asserted adjunction.
